headline: S&P 500 closed at 7,543.64 on Thursday as chips rebounded and oil retreated; Asian markets gained overnight on renewed AI optimism, but Iran-Strait of Hormuz risk and a looming Fed rate-hike debate keep the backdrop unsettled heading into Friday's open.
stance: Cautiously constructive — but carry your hard hat. Thursday's cash close was genuinely encouraging: semiconductors led a broad recovery and the 10-year yield eased back from its Wednesday spike near 4.58%. Overnight in Asia the Kospi surged 2.6% and European tech bounced, extending the momentum. The catch: oil is still priced for an active war zone (WTI prior cash close $71.81/bbl), the Fed minutes flagged persistent inflation, and markets are beginning to price in at least one rate hike before year-end — a headwind for a market sitting at a CAPE of 42x. Delta Air Lines reports Q2 before the open today and is the first real read on consumer travel spending under higher fuel costs; its guidance will colour airline and broader consumer-discretionary sentiment.

news.head: Iran escalation — ceasefire declared over
news.body: Trump declared the interim Iran ceasefire 'over' and the U.S. military confirmed strikes on Iran for a second straight day targeting Strait of Hormuz navigation capacity; Iran vowed large-scale retaliation, keeping energy-supply risk elevated.

news.head: Oil whipsawed — settled lower Thursday
news.body: WTI crude (prior cash close $71.81/bbl) and Brent (prior cash close $76.04/bbl) pulled back from the Wednesday 5%-plus surge as evidence emerged that laden tankers continued to transit the Strait of Hormuz despite fresh attacks.

news.head: Chips rebound on SK Hynix ADR fever
news.body: Micron gained ~4.5% and Sandisk popped 7.6% on Thursday; SK Hynix's U.S. ADR — the world's second-largest HBM chip maker — lists on Nasdaq today and was reportedly more than seven times oversubscribed, underscoring intense AI-infrastructure demand.

news.head: Fed minutes: few hike votes, but inflation worry grows
news.body: Minutes from the June FOMC meeting showed only a handful of officials favored an immediate rate increase, but the committee broadly flagged persistent inflation; markets are now pricing in at least one hike by year-end 2026.

news.head: Delta Air Lines Q2 earnings — before the open today
news.body: DAL reports Q2 this morning; the Street consensus is roughly $1.44–$1.49 EPS (a ~31% year-on-year decline driven by fuel costs), though Delta has beaten estimates in each of the past four quarters — guidance on fuel hedging and H2 capacity will be the key read-across for travel and energy.

news.head: Meta surges on proprietary AI chip plan
news.body: Meta gained roughly 4% Thursday after announcing it will target production of its own in-house AI chip by September, reducing its dependence on Nvidia and reinforcing the AI capex super-cycle narrative.

news.head: Dallas Fed President Logan speaks today
news.body: Logan, a 2026 FOMC voter, delivers remarks today — her comments on inflation and the rate path will be watched closely given the hawkish drift in Fed communication this week.

news.head: Jobless claims remain subdued
news.body: Initial jobless claims for the week ended July 4 came in at 215,000 — below the 218,000 consensus and the lowest print since late May — signalling a still-tight labour market that gives the Fed less reason to cut.

implications: Strait of Hormuz remains open but under active attack risk — not a confirmed closure — so the oil spike is pricing in a risk premium, not a supply disruption yet; a de-escalation headline could knock $5–8 off WTI quickly, while a confirmed closure could add $10–15.

The 10-year yield (prior cash close 4.56%) retreated from Wednesday's intraday high near 4.58% after a well-bid Treasury auction, suggesting bond buyers view current yields as attractive; watch 4.60% as near-term resistance that, if broken, would pressure equity valuations at current CAPE of 42x.

Semiconductor momentum is the market's load-bearing wall right now — SK Hynix's Nasdaq debut today is a live sentiment test; strong first-day trading would validate the AI-demand thesis and likely lift Nasdaq futures further.

Real rates at 2.31% and an equity risk premium of -2.05% mean stocks are historically expensive relative to risk-free alternatives — this does not cause a correction by itself, but it compresses the margin for error on earnings or Fed surprises.

The yen (prior cash close ¥162.32/$) sits at a 3-year extreme — the carry trade remains intact but intervention risk is elevated; a fast yen strengthening episode could trigger a disorderly unwind similar to mid-2024, with knock-on selling in U.S. equities.

Positioning: Speculators have almost no bullish bets left in Nasdaq 100 futures (4th percentile of 3 years) and Russell 2000 futures (2nd percentile) — a contrarian floor that historically limits downside and accelerates any rally as shorts cover. In contrast, speculators are heavily positioned in Copper futures (95th percentile) — a contrarian warning for the industrial-metals complex. High-yield bond positioning is also extended long (89th percentile) — credit investors should not expect spread compression to do much more heavy lifting from here.

watch.head: SK Hynix ADR first-day trade
watch.body: The ADR listing is a live read on institutional appetite for AI-memory names — watch the open price and volume; a strong debut would likely lift Micron and Broadcom sympathetically.

watch.head: Delta Q2 guidance (DAL, before open)
watch.body: EPS consensus ~$1.44–$1.49; the number matters less than the H2 fuel-cost and capacity guide — any upward revision to full-year outlook would be a positive signal for the consumer and airline sector.

watch.head: Dallas Fed's Logan on rates
watch.body: A 2026 FOMC voter; any language firming up the case for a 2026 hike would push the front end of the yield curve higher and weigh on rate-sensitive sectors like real estate and utilities.

watch.head: Strait of Hormuz headlines
watch.body: Any confirmed chokepoint closure or Iranian retaliation against U.S. bases would immediately reprice oil, yields, and gold — keep a news alert active throughout the session.

watch.head: June CPI — next Tuesday Jul 14
watch.body: The next major macro catalyst; Fed Chair Warsh also testifies to Congress on Tuesday — a hot CPI print combined with hawkish Warsh testimony would be the biggest near-term risk to the equity rally.

watch.head: Yen at ¥162/$
watch.body: USD/JPY (prior cash close ¥162.32/$) sits at a 99.5th percentile 3-year extreme; Japanese authorities have previously intervened near this level — a sudden yen rally could unwind carry trades and spike volatility broadly.

sections.title: Macro & Rates
bullets: 10-year Treasury yield: prior cash close 4.56%; 2-year yield: prior cash close 4.21% — the curve is positively sloped at +35 bps (10Y minus 2Y), a modest but meaningful shift from the inversion that persisted through much of 2024–2025.
10-year breakeven inflation (the bond market's inflation forecast) sits at 2.25% — above the Fed's 2% target and consistent with the June FOMC minutes' concern about persistent price pressures.

Real interest rates (inflation-adjusted) at 2.31% are meaningfully positive, which historically acts as a brake on speculative asset prices and gold; gold (prior cash close $4,132.60/oz) has pulled back from its January record near $5,600 but remains elevated at the 80th percentile of its 3-year range.

The Fed balance sheet is barely growing (+1.11% year-on-year) and the Treasury's cash account holds $774bn — no immediate liquidity injection expected, so markets must fund themselves from existing reserves of $3,099bn.

Financial conditions remain loose overall: the Chicago Fed's national financial conditions index is negative (meaning easier than average), and the St. Louis Fed stress index is negative at -0.72 — neither signals systemic stress.
ISM Manufacturing at 53.3 (above 50 = expansion) and Services at 54.5 both point to a still-growing economy, reducing the urgency for Fed cuts and supporting the higher-for-longer rate view.
sections.positioning: In 3-month SOFR futures — the market's main bet on where short-term interest rates go — speculators have almost no bullish bets left (1st percentile of 3 years, a contrarian floor suggesting the market has already priced in a great deal of rate pessimism).

sections.title: Equity Markets
bullets: Prior cash close: S&P 500 7,543.64; Nasdaq 100 26,206.89; Dow Jones 52,487.41 — all three indices recovered Thursday after Wednesday's Iran-driven selloff, with Nasdaq leading (+1.30%) on the chip rebound.

Overnight in Asia: MSCI Asia Pacific +0.5%, South Korea's Kospi +2.6% (partly SK Hynix-driven), Japan's Nikkei was +1.4% in Thursday's session — risk appetite is being rebuilt in the overnight session heading into the U.S. open.

Market breadth is improving but not yet dominant: 60.2% of S&P 500 stocks trade above their 50-day moving average and 65.1% above their 200-day — solid, but not the 80%+ reading that characterises the most powerful bull phases.

VIX (the S&P 500's 'fear gauge') closed at 15.84 — complacent by historical standards and a potential vulnerability if Iran headlines escalate sharply; VXN (Nasdaq volatility) at 26.91 is more elevated, reflecting ongoing uncertainty around AI valuations.
SKEW index at 144.7 indicates that sophisticated options traders are paying a meaningful premium to insure against a large, sudden drop — they are not complacent even if headline VIX looks calm.

CAPE ratio at 42x means the market is priced for near-perfection on earnings delivery; with the equity risk premium at -2.05% (stocks technically offering less return than risk-free bonds on a long-run basis), any earnings miss carries above-average punishment risk.

Meta's 4% Thursday gain on its proprietary AI chip announcement reinforces the theme that Big Tech is racing to reduce Nvidia dependency — a structural shift worth monitoring for semiconductor supply-chain implications.
sections.positioning: Speculators have almost no bullish bets left in Nasdaq 100 futures (4th percentile) and Russell 2000 futures (2nd percentile) — contrarian floors that historically cap the downside and create the conditions for a short-covering rally if positive catalysts arrive. VIX futures positioning is also at the 12th percentile (speculators are net short volatility protection) — a contrarian signal that the market could see a sharper vol spike than most expect if the Iran situation deteriorates.

single_name.note: CarMax Inc. (Consumer Cyclical) — company insiders have been buying, large off-exchange block buying (quiet institutional accumulation) is live, and a burst of unusual options buying has been detected; shorts are relatively heavy at 4.4 days-to-cover, creating squeeze risk if the stock moves higher. Signal is fresh as of Jul 8.

sections.title: Credit & Liquidity
bullets: High-yield credit spread over investment-grade: 270 bps — neither alarming nor tight; investment-grade spreads at 76 bps confirm that large investment-grade companies face no meaningful funding stress.
FRA-OIS and SOFR-OIS spreads (measures of stress in short-term bank funding markets) are both at -4 bps — essentially flat, meaning banks are funding themselves without any visible strain.
Commercial paper funding spread at 21 bps is benign — the short-term corporate borrowing market is open and cheap.
Bank credit growth at 6.33% year-on-year is healthy; syndicated loan rates at 7.02% reflect the higher-rate environment but have not choked off lending activity.

M2 money supply growing at 5.58% year-on-year provides a moderate liquidity tailwind for asset prices; the Fed's overnight reverse repo facility (where money-market funds park cash) has dwindled to just $5.8bn — essentially zero — meaning that pool of sideline cash has already been deployed into the market.

Equity-credit correlation at 0.70 means stocks and credit spreads are moving closely together — when they diverge (credit widening while stocks hold), it has historically been an early warning; currently both are stable.

single_name.note: Scorpio Tankers Inc. (Energy/Shipping) — company insiders have been buying, large off-exchange block buying is live, and a burst of unusual options buying is detected; the Strait of Hormuz situation directly affects tanker routing and day-rates, making this a live macro-linked setup. Shorts are modest at 4.0 days-to-cover. Signal is fresh as of Jul 8.
